## Natural history notes

A slender woodland ant characterized by its reddish-brown to brown body, long legs, narrow waist, and a distinctive notched ridge or “collar” feature on the head that gives the species its common name. In Florida, the Notched Collared Ant is associated with wooded habitats including xeric and mesic hammocks, longleaf pine savannas, and forested areas with fallen logs, leaf litter, and woody debris. Colonies may nest in logs or similar sheltered wood cavities, while workers forage through leaf litter for small insects, scavenged material, seeds, nectar, and honeydew, helping move nutrients and small food items through the forest-floor food web.
